_comment: Everything spoken in the first fifteen minutes. Text lives here and never in a script, so a rewrite of Grandpa's voice is a data edit and a translator never has to read GDScript.
_comment_shape: A conversation is a speaker, a portrait, and an ordered list of lines. NO branching: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md is explicit that the only choice in this sequence is which creature, and that one is made through scripts/ui/starter_picker.gd's orb preview, not a dialogue branch (SA0-orbs, 2026-08-11; before that it was made by walking up to a body in the meadow, which is what this comment used to describe). The previous prototype's DialogueRunner supported choices and this port deliberately drops them — the moment a line can branch, the starter choice starts wanting to be a text menu instead of something you look at first.
_comment_lines: A line is a string, or an object when it needs to override the speaker/portrait or emit an effect. Effects are opaque strings handed back to whoever started the conversation; this file knows that finishing the briefing emits `beat:starter_choice` and that the first-catch line emits `give:orb_basic:50`, and the dialogue system has no idea what a beat or an item is. A `give:` effect sits on the exact line that speaks the gift, so the satchel fills as he says it rather than in a lump after the box closes.
_comment_voice: He is warm and brief. The opening gives exactly one clear objective at a time: choose a starter, catch a second creature, see Mira, then sign up for the tournament.

grandpa_house._comment: Required first conversation. It establishes the immediate threat and moves directly into starter selection; later conversations teach the next action one at a time.
grandpa_house.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: They've taken Meadows Hall, and the land's already starting to suffer.
I'd go after them myself if I were twenty years younger.
If you're going to take this on, you won't do it alone.

lines.text: Come on. It's time you chose your first creature.

grandpa_waiting._comment: Talking to him again before choosing. Short on purpose: a player who came back to hear the briefing twice is a player the game is wasting. Practically unreachable since SA0-orbs -- the picker opens the instant this conversation closes and is modal, so there is no real window left to talk to him again mid-choice. Kept rather than deleted: harmless, and cheap insurance if the picker's timing ever changes.
grandpa_waiting.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Still deciding? Take your time — have another look at all three.

grandpa_first_catch._comment: The required return after naming. Grandpa's pack arrives here -- orbs, potions, berries, Revives -- just before its first use, rather than being buried in the starter exposition.
grandpa_first_catch._comment_gifts: The pack. All four gifts here are RESTORED, not new, and all four were dropped by the same commit. `66eb47ec` (2026-08-28, 'First-hour: sequence opening through tournament signup') reflowed this whole file and took `give:orb_basic:15`, `give:potion_small:3`, `give:berries:5` and `give:revive:2` off `grandpa_house` together, re-adding only the orbs. One-line commit message, no note anywhere, and nothing it contradicted was ever superseded: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md beat 3 still names the pack as 'orbs, potions, berries' and still spells the three effects out by name, D18 still calls it 'a parting gift of orbs and potions', and D40 added the Revives 'alongside the existing orbs/potions/berries'. `git log -S "give:potion" -- data/dialogue/opening.json` finds the add and that one silent removal and nothing else; the same for `give:berr` and `give:revive`.
grandpa_first_catch._comment_gifts_cost: Each half of the removal cost a Gate F capstone run its chapter. CAP-1 (ralph/reports/FINDING-CAP1-TUTORIAL-CATCH-FAINT-2026-08-31.md) was the Revives: a FAINTED starter with nothing in the satchel able to raise it. CAP-2 (ralph/reports/FINDING-CAP2-NO-HEAL-FOR-LIVING-DAMAGE-2026-08-31.md) is the potions: a LIVING starter carried out of the tutorial at 53.0 of 117.6 with nothing able to top it up, into a village training fight it then lost. A Revive refuses a creature that has not fainted (D40) and CAP-1's faint floor is gated on `party.all_fainted()`, so neither answer covers ordinary battle damage -- and the only other full heal in the game is a creature bed, a buildable whose fiber is past tools the player does not have yet.
grandpa_first_catch._comment_gifts_placement: All four sit here rather than on `grandpa_house` where D40 and OPENING_SEQUENCE.md put them, for the reason `66eb47ec` moved the orbs: a `give:` effect belongs on the beat before its first possible use, not in a briefing three beats earlier. Order is the pack's original order -- orbs, potions, berries, Revives -- which is also hurt, fed, fallen.
grandpa_first_catch._comment_orb_count: TUNABLE, owner directive: raised 15 -> 50. `tournament.json`'s `min_party_size` is 5 -- a full five-creature team, not the three the village tutorial ladder alone builds -- and the starter is only one of those five, so the tutorial's own catch plus building the rest of the roster before sign-up draws on this same supply. 15 was measured tight: even the tutorial's own bramblebun, given the highest catch_rate in species.json specifically so its catch cannot fail twice, still cost 2-4 landed-throw attempts in practice, before any of the other four team members are caught at ordinary (lower) catch rates. 50 leaves real room to miss and still reach the tournament with a full team, without touching catch odds/accuracy (GAME_DESIGN.md 15's affordability rule) or making orb_greater/orb_prime redundant, since they stay strictly better per throw.
grandpa_first_catch.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Before you go anywhere, you need another creature beside you.

lines.text: Take these Orbs. Head outside, find one you like, and catch it.
Three potions. For your creature, mind — you get soup.
Berries off my bushes. A fed creature forgives a long day.
And two Revives, at the bottom. A creature that's gone down won't get up on its own — don't waste them.
Then come back and show me.

grandpa_encounter_hint._comment: Talking to him between the naming and the catch. He does not repeat the whole briefing.
grandpa_encounter_hint.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Down the path, past the rise. Get close and it'll stop and look at you — that's your moment.

grandpa_after_first_catch._comment: The required return after the first catch. Mira owns the tool/recipe reward; this only points the player to her.
grandpa_after_first_catch._comment_training_line: OWNER-0901-TRAIN-CLARITY. Owner playtest 2026-09-01 item 7/10: 'still unclear how to train a team... no clear guidance on what training is or how to do it' -- a repeat of the same complaint from 2026-08-30B item 17. The only existing answer was objectives.json's `tournament_train_team` `how` line ('Villagers who offer a fight are the training'), which only shows inside the Quest Log tab (quest_log.gd's `tracked_hint()` is deliberately not wired to the HUD -- see that function's own header) and only once the player has already opened a menu to find it. This line puts the same fact in the one dialogue box every player is required to read this early -- the conversation that gates `beat:visit_mira` -- so the mechanic is established before the tournament's own checklist (Halda's registrar line, OWNER-0901-TOURNAMENT-LEVEL5's scope, not this one) ever has to re-teach it.
grandpa_after_first_catch.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Nice catch. That's how a team starts.
Fight with it from here on — wild creatures, other trainers, whoever's willing. Win, and it grows stronger. That's all training is.
Now go see Mira in the village. She'll give you some basic tools and teach you how to make more Orbs.

grandpa_tournament._comment: The required return after Mira. The registrar owns the qualification explanation and the broadened checklist.
grandpa_tournament.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Good. Now you can take care of yourself out there.
If you really want to go after Team Tether, start by proving you can handle a team.
Go sign up for the village tournament.

lines.text: They'll tell you what you need to enter.
